doc.title: Dan Morgenstern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 9, 2013

title: The liner note writer's obligation to the listener
summary: He explains that notes should enhance listening by identifying soloists, tempos and each track, which DJs appreciated.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: So you try to make — but most of all I think the obligation of the liner notes’ writer is to try to enhance the listening experience for the listener. And so I think one thing that’s important is to identify soloists when they’re not obvious, mostly when it comes to a band performance. Or if there are two people playing the same instrument or whatever, and to point out certain things that might be helpful. And again I found that people have told me that this was indeed so, I mean that they learned something from — and my biggest fans actually for a long time in the days when there were many more jazz DJs than there are now, I sometimes would get notes and things from DJs saying how much they appreciated that I, unlike a lot of other liner note writers, I would say something about each cut on the album and I would say things like who was soloing, and also what the tempo was if something was a ballad or an uptempo thing or whatever. Because they said very often they didn’t have time — a new record would come in and they wouldn’t have time to listen to all of it and this way —
